title: The Thirteenth Floor
narration: My building has twelve floors, but last night the lift stopped at thirteen. The corridor copied my home, including photographs of me living with strangers. An older version of me pressed a bloodstained key into my hand and warned me about her husband. When I escaped downstairs, my husband said his key no longer worked. The bloodstained key opened our flat, where every family photograph now showed him beside the older woman. Every explanation I tried made the details worse, because each clue had been placed where I alone would find it. I wanted to leave immediately, but doing that would mean abandoning the only proof that any of this had happened. The silence felt deliberate, as though someone nearby was waiting for me to understand the trap before moving again. In every picture, I was outside the window, watching them.
